hr_005:n1.prompt:
You are helping me process an employee termination in our payroll platform, {{vendor}}, as part of offboarding. Before starting, ask me for: the departing employee's full name/ID, last day of employment, termination reason/type (voluntary/involuntary), final pay details (regular wages owed, unused PTO payout if applicable per state law, any bonus/commission owed), and whether this requires an off-cycle payroll run outside the normal schedule.

Using {{vendor}}'s dashboard or documented public API with my configured credentials, please:
1. Locate the employee's record in {{vendor}}.
2. Prepare the termination entry with the last day of employment and termination reason.
3. Prepare the final paycheck calculation, including any off-cycle payroll run needed to pay out final wages, PTO, or bonuses on time.
4. If a regular payroll run is already scheduled/submitted for this employee and needs to be cancelled or corrected before disbursement, prepare that correction.
5. Note any linked benefits (health insurance enrollment) that will need deduction changes synced to payroll as part of termination, without making changes outside payroll itself.
6. Compile a summary showing: employee name, last day, final pay breakdown, payroll run type (regular vs off-cycle), and any corrections/cancellations needed.

Do not submit, finalize, or apply any termination, payroll cancellation, or off-cycle run in {{vendor}} — a human must explicitly approve these changes before they are applied. Present the full prepared summary and explicitly stop for human sign-off once everything is ready for review.

Report back with: the prepared termination details, final pay calculation, any payroll cancellation/correction needed, and confirmation that you are awaiting my explicit approval before applying anything in {{vendor}}.

hr_005:n2.prompt: You are helping me calculate a departing employee's final paycheck and PTO payout in {{vendor}}, our payroll platform, as part of offboarding. If any of the following are missing, ask me for them: employee legal name, termination date, last day worked, state (for final-pay timing rules), accrued/unused PTO balance, any bonuses or corrections owed, and confirmation that PTO payout policy applies. Using my configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and: (1) create a new off-cycle payroll run scoped to this one employee to calculate their final regular wages plus PTO payout, entering the termination date, last worked date, and PTO hours/balance as configured in our PTO policy; (2) retrieve and review the calculated payroll data (gross pay, PTO payout amount, taxes, deductions, net pay) before anything is finalized; (3) flag any discrepancies versus the inputs I gave you (e.g., PTO balance mismatch, missing off-cycle reason, wrong pay date). Prepare a clear summary showing: employee name, termination date, gross final pay, PTO payout amount and hours, deductions, and net pay, plus the direct deposit method and expected pay date (noting if fast/next-day deposit is available and being used). Do NOT submit, approve, or finalize the off-cycle payroll run — this requires my explicit sign-off before any payment is issued. Once you've built the draft run and pulled the review data, stop for human sign-off and present me the summary along with a direct link or clear instructions for where I go in {{vendor}} to review and approve it myself. Report back with the draft payroll details, any flagged issues, and confirmation that the run is staged but not yet approved.

hr_005:n3.prompt:
You are helping me terminate benefits for a departing employee as part of our offboarding process, using {{vendor}} (our payroll/benefits platform). Approval is required before any change is applied, so you must prepare everything but stop short of finalizing.

If you don't already have it, ask me for: the employee's full name, their last day of employment/termination date, whether COBRA or state continuation notices are required, and any benefit-specific end-date rules (e.g., health coverage runs to end of month vs. immediate cutoff).

Then, using your configured credentials to access {{vendor}}:
1. Locate the employee's profile and pull up their current health insurance enrollment and 401(k)/retirement plan participation.
2. Prepare the termination of health insurance enrollment effective on the correct date, noting how it will affect payroll deductions going forward.
3. Prepare the termination of 401(k)/retirement plan contributions so no further payroll-synced contributions occur after the final paycheck.
4. Draft a summary showing: current enrollments, proposed end dates for each benefit, and the payroll deduction changes that will result.
5. Note any COBRA or continuation-of-coverage notice that will need to be triggered, if applicable, and prepare that documentation for review (but do not send it).

Do not submit, confirm, or apply any termination changes in {{vendor}} — only stage/draft them so a human can review the exact effective dates and deduction impacts.

When done, report back with: the employee's name, the benefits identified (health insurance, 401k/retirement), the proposed termination effective dates for each, the resulting payroll deduction changes, and any COBRA/continuation notice prepared. Clearly state that this is prepared and ready, and stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied in {{vendor}}.

hr_005:n4.prompt:
You are helping me offboard a departing employee by deactivating their email account in {{vendor}}, our email platform. Approval is required before any change is applied, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for any missing details you need: the departing employee's full name and email address, their departure/last-working date, whether their mailbox contents or emails need to be preserved or forwarded (and to whom, if so), and who the approver is for this action.

Using your configured credentials, access our {{vendor}} admin console and locate the employee's account. Prepare a clear summary that includes: the account to be suspended, current account status, any active email forwarding or delegation settings, mailbox size/data considerations, and a recommended plan (e.g., suspend account, set up auto-forward or delegate access to a manager if requested, and schedule eventual deletion per our retention policy).

Do not suspend, deactivate, or modify the account yourself. Present the prepared plan and summary to the designated approver and stop for human sign-off. Do not click any confirm/apply button, submit any change, or approve the action on my behalf under any circumstances.

Once you have prepared the summary, report back to me with: the employee's account details, the proposed deactivation/forwarding plan, any risks or open questions (e.g., unresolved mailbox contents), and confirmation that the action is paused awaiting explicit human approval. If you cannot locate the account or need clarification on data handling preferences, flag that in your report rather than proceeding.

hr_005:n5.prompt:
You are helping me offboard a departing employee by removing them from our team chat tool, {{vendor}}. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) the employee's full name and the email or username associated with their {{vendor}} account, (2) the effective date/time the removal should occur, and (3) whether any of their channels, direct messages, or shared files need to be preserved, exported, or transferred to a manager before removal.

Once I provide these details, please:
1. Locate the employee's account in {{vendor}} using your configured credentials.
2. Confirm their current status (active member, admin rights, channel memberships, connected integrations or bots they own).
3. Prepare a clear removal plan: what will happen when the account is deactivated/removed (loss of access, message retention per our workspace settings, any ownership transfers needed for channels or integrations they administer).
4. If they own any channels, shared workflows, or integrations, draft a list of these along with a recommended new owner, but do not reassign anything yet.
5. Draft the exact removal action you intend to take (e.g., "Deactivate/remove [name] from the {{vendor}} workspace effective [date]") and compile it into a short summary along with the ownership-transfer list.

Because this step requires a human to explicitly approve before changes are applied, do not remove, deactivate, or modify the account yourself. Present me with the complete removal plan, the account status findings, and any ownership-transfer recommendations, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the employee's account details found, the prepared removal action, the list of channels/integrations needing ownership transfer (if any), and a note confirming you are awaiting my explicit approval before proceeding.

hr_005:n6.prompt:
You are helping me offboard a departing employee from our code hosting organization ({{vendor}}). This action requires explicit human approval before any changes are applied, so you must prepare everything and then stop.

If you don't already have it, ask me for: the departing employee's full name, their {{vendor}} username or email, and our organization/workspace name on {{vendor}}.

Using your configured credentials, please:
1. Look up the employee's membership status in our {{vendor}} organization, including their role/permission level and any teams, repositories, or projects they have access to.
2. Identify any personal access tokens, SSH keys, or two-factor authentication devices registered under their account that are tied to organizational access.
3. Check for any repository-level or branch-level permissions granted specifically to this user outside their general org membership.
4. Compile a clear removal plan listing: the account to be removed, all teams/repos they'll be removed from, and any tokens or keys that should be revoked as part of this offboarding.
5. Present this plan to me in a summary report, formatted as a checklist, so I can review exactly what will change.

Do NOT remove the user from the organization, revoke tokens, delete SSH keys, or make any other changes yet. Once you've prepared the full removal plan and checklist, stop for human sign-off. I will review and explicitly approve before you (or I) execute the actual removal via the dashboard or API.

When done, report back with: the employee's current access summary, the proposed removal checklist, and a clear note that you are awaiting my approval before applying any changes.

hr_005:n7.prompt:
You are helping me complete step hr_005:n7 of our employee offboarding process: notifying a departing employee about their equity exercise window. This step requires a human to explicitly approve before any changes are applied — you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

First, ask me for any missing inputs you need:
- The departing employee's name and personal email (for post-termination contact)
- Their last day of employment / termination date
- The equity management platform we use ({{vendor}}) and confirmation you have access via my configured credentials
- Our standard post-termination exercise window policy (e.g., 90 days) if it varies by grant type

Then, using {{vendor}}:
1. Look up the employee's equity grant records — vested shares, unvested/forfeited shares, strike price(s), and grant dates.
2. Determine the exact post-termination exercise deadline based on their termination date and our policy, per grant if terms differ.
3. Draft a clear notification email to the employee explaining: what they have vested, the exercise deadline (specific date), how to exercise through their {{vendor}} portal, and a plain-language summary of tax treatment and what happens to unvested shares.
4. Prepare a summary record for internal HR/finance showing the employee's name, vested share count, strike price, exercise deadline, and grant IDs.
5. Flag any grants with unusual terms (e.g., accelerated vesting clauses, extended exercise windows) that may need special handling.

Do not send the notification email or make any changes to grant status in {{vendor}} — only prepare the draft email and the summary record.

When done, report back: the employee's grant summary, the calculated exercise deadline(s), the drafted notification email text, and any flagged exceptions. Then stop for human sign-off before the email is sent or any records are modified.

hr_005:n8.prompt:
You are helping me prepare and track the 'collect company property' step for an offboarding employee. Physical retrieval of laptops, badges, keys, phones, and other equipment is an in-person handoff and remains a human step — you cannot perform it yourself.

First, ask me for anything you need: the departing employee's name and last working day, the list of company property issued to them (check our asset inventory or onboarding records if I have one, e.g. a spreadsheet or IT asset system name), the manager or HR contact responsible for the physical exchange, and my preferred communication tool (email, Slack, etc.).

Then do the following preparation work:
1. Compile a clear checklist of all property to be returned, based on the inventory or records I provide.
2. Draft a reminder message/email to the departing employee specifying what to return, where, and by when, plus a copy for their manager/HR contact to coordinate logistics.
3. Prepare a simple confirmation/sign-off form or tracking log (item, returned Y/N, date, condition, verifier) that the on-site person can fill in during the handoff.
4. Set up a follow-up reminder for me to check status after the expected return date, since this is an async step whose result lands later — note explicitly that I'll need to poll/verify completion once the physical handoff has happened.

Do not attempt to confirm, mark complete, or close out the property return yourself — the actual collection is a physical exchange and remains a human step.

Report back with: the completed checklist, the drafted messages, the tracking/confirmation form, and a note on when/how I should check back to verify the property was returned.
